status: drafted via multi-agent workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text, adversarially fact-checked and corrected
notes: GROUNDING METHOD: read the full 36-chapter Ethiopian translation text at Assets/Resources/Verses/Ethiopian/2_chronicles_14.json chapter-by-chapter (all 822 verses) before drafting, then cross-checked against the already-completed KJV Character Index for this book for structural comparison. REAL FINDING (not assumed, verified by direct comparison): for 2 Chronicles specifically, this "Ethiopian" translation's English text is essentially word-for-word IDENTICAL to the KJV wording across all 36 chapters - same verse divisions, same names, same numbers, same theological content, same narrative order, no additions/omissions/reordering detected anywhere in the book. This is a genuine per-book finding, not an assumption carried over from other books in this project (where real differences HAVE been found, e.g. this same Ethiopian Bible's own 9-chapter 1-Esdras-style "Ezra") - 2 Chronicles simply is not one of the books where this source diverges from the standard Masoretic/KJV textual tradition. Because the underlying text is identical, the scribe-tier/manager/submanager structure below intentionally mirrors the validated KJV 2Chronicles.json structure (29 tiers, all person-type - this is royal narrative history throughout, no law/theme tiers needed) rather than inventing a different structure for its own sake; all ids are freshly suffixed "_eth" to avoid any collision with the KJV CharacterIndex's ids or a future Geneva-translation pass, per the schema's collision-avoidance instruction. NAMING-COLLISION CENSUS (re-verified against this translation's own text, all present exactly as in KJV): four uses of "Azariah" (son of Oded 15:1; the chief priest confronting Uzziah 26:17-20; son of Johanan among Ahaz's-era Ephraimite leaders 28:12; plus Ahaziah of Judah's own text variant "Azariah the son of Jehoram" at 22:6); three "Zechariah"s (son of Jehoiada; Uzziah's instructing seer 26:5; Jahaziel's ancestor 20:14) plus a fourth purely genealogical mention as Hezekiah's maternal grandfather (29:1); "Jehoram"/"Joram" used interchangeably for two contemporaries in 21:5-22:7 (Jehoram of Judah and Jehoram/Joram of Israel, Ahab's son - 22:5 uses both spellings for the Israelite king within one verse, exactly as in KJV); "Jehoahaz" used for both Ahaziah of Judah (21:17, alternate name) and Josiah's three-month son (36:1-4); "Joash"/"Jehoash" used for both Joash king of Judah and Joash king of Israel who defeats Amaziah (25:17-24); "Manasseh" used as a tribal/territorial name (31:1, 34:6) distinct from King Manasseh; Athaliah called "the daughter of Ahab" at 21:6 but "the daughter of Omri" (Ahab's father) at 22:2, a hedged crux; Michaiah (Abijah's mother, 13:2) is a near-homograph of the unrelated prophet Micaiah (18:4ff); Jehoiachin's age at accession is given as "eight years old" (36:9), a well-known crux against 2 Kings 24:8's "eighteen"; Zedekiah is called Jehoiachin's "brother" at 36:10 though genealogically his uncle. All hedged exactly as this translation's own text presents them, never silently resolved. The craftsman "Huram his father" (4:16) is confirmed in this translation's own literal wording, sharing his name with King Huram of Tyre who sent him. Huram's restoration of cities TO Solomon (8:1-2) is confirmed as this book's own direction, distinct from 1 Kings 9:10-13's account.

characters.name: Solomon

verses.note: Asks God for wisdom at Gibeon rather than riches.
Builds and dedicates the Temple; fire from heaven consumes the sacrifice (7:1).
Visited by the Queen of Sheba.
Reigns 40 years, dies, succeeded by Rehoboam.

funFacts: Wisdom-request and Temple-building both original to this arc, confirmed word-for-word matching KJV in this translation.

characters.name: Huram, King of Tyre

verses.note: Correspondence with Solomon; supplies cedar/fir/algum timber and sends the craftsman "Huram his father."
"The cities which Huram had restored to Solomon, Solomon built them" - Huram gives cities TO Solomon, confirmed exactly as this translation reads it.
His servants, with Solomon's, bring gold and algum trees from Ophir; joint navy to Tarshish.

funFacts: Shares the name "Huram" with the craftsman he personally sends to Solomon (2:13) - intra-book collision, king and craftsman.

genealogy.mother: a woman of the daughters of Dan (2:14)

verses.note: Sent by King Huram, "endued with understanding," skilled in gold, silver, brass, iron, stone, timber, and engraving.
Makes the pots, shovels, fleshhooks, and all the bronze Temple furnishings; called "Huram his father" throughout, confirmed as this translation's own literal wording.
Tests Solomon with hard questions, is overwhelmed by his wisdom and the Temple, blesses the LORD.
Exchanges gifts with Solomon; gives gold, spices, and precious stones.
Rejects the elders' counsel, answers the people harshly; ten tribes revolt under Jeroboam.
Fortifies Judah's cities; large family.
Forsakes the law of the LORD; Shishak of Egypt invades; Shemaiah's word; Rehoboam humbles himself.
Stops Rehoboam from attacking the ten tribes: "this thing is done of me."
Tells Rehoboam and the princes, fleeing before Shishak, that God has given them up because they forsook Him; they humble themselves.
Invades Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year with a vast Egyptian/Libyan/Sukkiim/Ethiopian army; takes the Temple and palace treasures, including Solomon's gold shields.

children: a son named Abijah, per 1 Kings 14 - not detailed in this book's own text

verses.note: Returns from Egypt, becomes leader of the ten northern tribes after Rehoboam's harsh answer.
Wars against Abijah of Judah at Zemaraim; loses despite an ambush; struck by the LORD, dies (13:20).

characters.name: Abijah

genealogy.mother: Michaiah, the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah (13:2)

verses.note: Defeats Jeroboam at Zemaraim after a covenant-themed speech; 500,000 Israelite soldiers slain, per this translation's own round number.

funFacts: His mother's name "Michaiah" (13:2) is a near-homograph of the unrelated prophet Micaiah (18:4ff) - different people.

verses.note: Removes idols; defeats Zerah the Ethiopian's massive army at Mareshah.
Reforms the kingdom after Azariah son of Oded's prophecy.
Allies with Syria against Israel instead of trusting God; rebuked by Hanani, imprisons him; diseased feet in old age; dies.

characters.name: Zerah the Ethiopian

verses.note: Invades with "a thousand thousand" and 300 chariots; routed by Asa's army with the LORD's help.

funFacts: Notable that this Ethiopian-tradition translation's own text names the invader "Zerah the Ethiopian" exactly as KJV does - not softened or altered.

characters.name: Azariah the son of Oded

verses.note: Meets Asa after the Zerah victory; "the LORD is with you, while ye be with him"; prompts covenant renewal.

funFacts: Distinct from the later prophet Oded (28:9) - do not conflate the two Odeds.

verses.note: Rebukes Asa for relying on Syria's king rather than the LORD; Asa imprisons him in a rage.

characters.name: Jehoshaphat

verses.note: Strengthens Judah, sends teachers of the law throughout the land.
Allies with Ahab of Israel by marriage; joins him at Ramoth-gilead against Micaiah's warning.
Rebuked by Jehu the seer; institutes judicial reforms.
Delivered from a Moabite/Ammonite coalition after Jahaziel's word; the battle is the LORD's.
Allies with Ahaziah king of Israel on a doomed Tarshish shipbuilding venture; condemned by Eliezer; the ships are broken.

funFacts: His alliances with the northern kingdom are each rebuked by a different prophet in turn - Micaiah, Jehu, and Eliezer.

genealogy.father: Omri (well known from Kings, not detailed in this book's own text)
children: a daughter, Athaliah, given in marriage to Jehoram of Judah (21:6)

verses.note: Persuades Jehoshaphat to join him against Ramoth-gilead.
Disguises himself in battle but is struck by a random arrow and dies, as Micaiah foretold.

characters.name: Micaiah the son of Imla

verses.note: Summoned at Jehoshaphat's request; alone among the prophets predicts Ahab's death; struck by Zedekiah son of Chenaanah; imprisoned on bread and water.

funFacts: Not to be confused with Michaiah, Abijah's mother (13:2) - different name-spelling, different person, different gender.

characters.name: Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah

verses.note: Makes iron horns, prophesies Ahab's victory over Syria.
Strikes Micaiah on the cheek after being contradicted.

funFacts: Shares the name "Zedekiah" with the final king of Judah (ch.36) - unrelated person.

genealogy.father: Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph (20:14)

verses.note: "The battle is not yours, but God's"; instructs Judah not to fight but to stand still and see the LORD's salvation.
Meets Jehoshaphat on his return from Ramoth-gilead: "Shouldest thou help the ungodly...wrath is upon thee."
Cited as the source recording "the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat."
"Because thou hast joined thyself with Ahaziah, the LORD hath broken thy works"; the Tarshish ships are wrecked and never sail.

characters.name: Ahaziah, King of Israel

verses.note: Joins Jehoshaphat to "make ships to go to Tarshish"; the ships are broken and never make the voyage.

funFacts: CRITICAL: distinct from Ahaziah, King of Judah (ch.22, its own manager tier) - Ahab's son, one generation earlier.

characters.name: Jehoram (Joram), King of Judah

children: several older sons, killed by Arabian/Philistine raiders (21:17)

verses.note: Murders his brothers upon taking the throne.
Walks in the ways of the kings of Israel because of his marriage to Athaliah; Edom and Libnah revolt.
Receives a written condemnation from Elijah.
Raided by Philistines/Arabians, who kill his sons and wives except Ahaziah; dies of an incurable bowel disease; "departed without being desired," not buried in the sepulchres of the kings.

funFacts: FLAGGED: shares the name "Jehoram"/"Joram" with his contemporary and brother-in-law, Jehoram king of Israel, Ahab's son - both names used for both men across 21:5-22:7 in this translation exactly as in KJV.

characters.name: Elijah the Prophet

verses.note: Sends a letter pronouncing a plague on Jehoram's people, wives, and goods, and a bowel disease on Jehoram himself.

funFacts: His famous 1 Kings ministry is not retold here; only this one letter appears.

characters.name: Ahaziah, King of Judah

verses.note: Made king after his brothers are slain; walks in the counsel of Ahab's house through his mother Athaliah.
Joins Jehoram of Israel against Hazael of Syria at Ramoth-gilead; visits the wounded Jehoram at Jezreel; his death there is "of God."
Found hiding in Samaria and killed by Jehu (of Nimshi).

funFacts: Also called "Jehoahaz" at 21:17, and this translation's own text at 22:6 literally reads "Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah" for this same Ahaziah - confirmed present verbatim, matching KJV's known textual variant.
CRITICAL: distinct from Ahaziah, King of Israel (ch.20, Ahab's son, a full generation earlier).

verses.note: Wounded by the Syrians at Ramoth-gilead; called "Jehoram" and "Joram" for the same person within these two verses, confirmed present in this translation exactly as in KJV.
Visited by Ahaziah of Judah at Jezreel, precipitating Ahaziah's own death.

characters.name: Athaliah

verses.note: Her counsel leads her son Ahaziah into wickedness.
On Ahaziah's death, destroys all the royal seed of Judah and reigns 6 years, except that Jehoshabeath hides the infant Joash.
Discovers the coronation of Joash, cries "Treason," is put to death at the horse gate entrance.

funFacts: CRUX confirmed present in this translation: 21:6 calls her "the daughter of Ahab" but 22:2 calls her "the daughter of Omri," Ahab's father - hedged, not resolved.

characters.name: Jehoiada the Priest

verses.note: His wife Jehoshabeath hides the infant Joash in the house of God.
Orchestrates the covenant and coronation of the seven-year-old Joash, arranges Athaliah's death, destroys the house of Baal.
Guides Joash's early, faithful reign; arranges two wives for him.
Dies at 130, is buried among the kings "because he had done good in Israel."

funFacts: Effectively co-regent/regent for the boy-king Joash - promoted to his own tier since his actions are the load-bearing hinge of the Athaliah-to-Joash transition.

verses.note: Steals the infant Joash from among the king's sons about to be slain and hides him in the Temple for six years.

characters.name: Joash

verses.note: Crowned at 7; under Jehoiada's guidance, repairs the Temple through a collected offering.
After Jehoiada's death, turns to idolatry at the princes' urging.
Has Zechariah, Jehoiada's own son, stoned in the Temple court.
Judah invaded by Syria; Joash is wounded, then killed in his bed by his own servants; not buried in the sepulchres of the kings.

funFacts: CRITICAL: shares the name "Joash"/"Jehoash" with Joash, King of Israel, who later defeats Amaziah.

verses.note: Invades Judah and Jerusalem; destroys the princes; Judah's small army defeats a much larger Syrian force "because they had forsaken the LORD."
Conspires against and kills Joash in his bed; confirmed named "Zabad" in this translation's own text, matching KJV (contrast "Jozachar" in the 2 Kings parallel).
Conspires with Zabad against and kills Joash.

characters.name: Zechariah, son of Jehoiada

genealogy.mother: Jehoshabeath (probable, as Jehoiada's wife, though not stated explicitly)

verses.note: Rebukes Joash and the princes for forsaking the LORD; stoned by the king's command in the court of the LORD's house; dying words, "The LORD look upon it, and require it."

funFacts: Promoted to his own tier: his murder is the direct narrative pivot bringing judgment on Joash's reign (24:24-25).

verses.note: Executes his father's murderers but spares their children per the law of Moses.
Hires, then dismisses, Israelite mercenaries at an unnamed man of God's word; defeats Edom, brings back their gods.
Rebuked by an unnamed prophet for worshipping Edom's gods; provokes and is defeated by Joash of Israel.
Conspired against, flees to Lachish, is killed there.

characters.name: Joash (Jehoash), King of Israel

genealogy.father: Jehoahaz of Israel (well known from Kings, not detailed in this book's own text)

verses.note: Answers Amaziah's challenge to battle with the fable of the thistle and the cedar.
Defeats and captures Amaziah at Bethshemesh, breaks down part of Jerusalem's wall, plunders the Temple and takes hostages.

funFacts: CRITICAL: shares the name "Joash" with Joash, King of Judah - a different person, one generation earlier.

verses.note: Prospers greatly "as long as he sought the LORD"; builds, farms, and strengthens the army.
Grows proud, unlawfully burns incense in the Temple, is struck with leprosy and confronted by Azariah the priest and 80 priests.
Lives out his days a leper, buried in a field belonging to the kings, "for they said, He is a leper."

characters.name: Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God

verses.note: "He sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God: and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him to prosper."

funFacts: A THIRD distinct "Zechariah" in this book, alongside Zechariah son of Jehoiada and Jahaziel's ancestor Zechariah (20:14).

characters.name: Azariah the Priest

verses.note: Goes in with 80 priests to withstand Uzziah's unlawful incense offering; leprosy breaks out on Uzziah's forehead as they confront him.

funFacts: One of THREE distinct "Azariah"s in this book (see the notes field).

verses.note: Builds the high gate of the Temple, fortifies cities, defeats the Ammonites and exacts tribute; "became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the LORD."

characters.name: Ahaz

verses.note: Walks in the ways of Israel's kings, makes molten images, burns his children in the fire.
Defeated by Syria and by Pekah, king of Israel, who kills 120,000 in one day and takes captives.
Appeals to Assyria for help, which distresses rather than strengthens him; shuts up the Temple doors.

funFacts: The Israelite army's captive-release, prompted by Oded and four named Ephraimite leaders, happens within his reign (28:9-15).

characters.name: Oded the Prophet

verses.note: Meets Israel's army returning to Samaria with Judahite captives; "deliver again the captives... for the fierce wrath of the LORD is upon you."

funFacts: Distinct from the earlier Azariah the son of Oded (15:1) - not assumed to be his father.

characters.name: Azariah the son of Johanan

verses.note: One of the heads of the children of Ephraim who "stood up against them that came from the war" and insisted the captives be released.

funFacts: A SECOND "Azariah" in this book, alongside Azariah son of Oded and Azariah the priest.

verses.note: Named among the four Ephraimite leaders opposing bringing the captives into Samaria.
Named among the four Ephraimite leaders opposing bringing the captives into Samaria.

characters.name: Amasa the son of Hadlai

verses.note: Named among the four Ephraimite leaders opposing bringing the captives into Samaria.

funFacts: Not the unrelated Amasa of 2 Samuel/1 Chronicles, David's general.

verses.note: Cleanses and reopens the Temple in his first year.
Celebrates a great Passover, inviting even the remnant of the northern tribes.
Organizes priestly/Levitical courses and tithes; destroys high places "in Ephraim also and Manasseh" - a territorial, not personal, use.
Withstands Sennacherib's invasion; prepares Jerusalem's defenses and the water conduit.
Falls sick and recovers; pride and the Babylonian envoys; dies, buried "in the chiefest of the sepulchres."

genealogy.father: Amoz (well known from Isaiah 1:1, not restated here)

verses.note: Prays together with Hezekiah against Sennacherib's threat.
Cited as recording "the rest of the acts of Hezekiah" in his vision.
Invades Judah, besieges the fenced cities; Hezekiah prepares Jerusalem's defenses and rallies the people.
Sends servants to blaspheme the LORD and urge surrender.
The LORD sends an angel who destroys his army; he returns home in shame.

Slain by "them that came forth of his own bowels" in the house of his god - names not given, confirmed as this translation's own sparser wording, matching KJV rather than 2 Kings 19:37's fuller account.

characters.name: Manasseh

verses.note: Extreme idolatry: rebuilds high places, sets up altars to Baal, makes his children pass through fire, uses divination.
Carried in fetters to Babylon by Assyrian captains; humbles himself greatly, prays, and is restored to his kingdom.
Fortifies cities, removes the idols, repairs the altar of the LORD after his repentance.

funFacts: FLAGGED: "Manasseh" also names a tribal territory in this book (31:1, 34:6), distinct from King Manasseh.

verses.note: Reigns 2 years, does evil like his father before Manasseh's repentance but "humbled not himself... as Manasseh his father had humbled himself"; killed by his own servants in his house.
The people of the land kill the conspirators and make Josiah king in his place.

children: Zedekiah (called Jehoiachin's "brother" at 36:10, though genealogically Josiah's son)

verses.note: Begins seeking God at 16, purges idolatry from Judah and "in the cities of Manasseh, and Ephraim, and Simeon" (territorial use, not the king) at 20.
Repairs the Temple; Hilkiah finds the book of the law; Shaphan reads it to the king.
Sends a delegation, including Hilkiah and Shaphan, to inquire of the LORD; Huldah the prophetess delivers her oracle.
Celebrates the greatest Passover "since the days of Samuel the prophet."
Disguises himself to fight Necho of Egypt at Megiddo despite Necho's warning; is mortally wounded and dies.
Jeremiah laments for him; the lamentation becomes an ordinance in Israel.
Finds "the book of the law of the LORD given by Moses" in the Temple.
Sent, with others, to inquire of the LORD concerning the book.

children: Ahikam (34:20, part of the same delegation to Huldah)

verses.note: Receives the book from Hilkiah and reads it before the king.
Sent with Hilkiah and others to inquire of the LORD.

characters.name: Huldah the Prophetess

spouses: Shallum the son of Tikvah, keeper of the wardrobe (34:22)

verses.note: Delivers the LORD's oracle: judgment is coming on Judah, but not in Josiah's own days, because his heart was tender.

funFacts: The only prophetess given a full recorded oracle in 2 Chronicles.

verses.note: Laments for Josiah; his lamentations are still referenced "in the lamentations" as an ongoing ordinance.
Zedekiah does not humble himself before Jeremiah, "speaking from the mouth of the LORD."
His word about the land's sabbaths/seventy years is fulfilled by Cyrus's decree.

characters.name: Pharaoh Necho, King of Egypt

verses.note: Warns Josiah not to fight him at Megiddo ("I come not against thee this day... forbear thee from meddling with God"); Josiah is mortally wounded in the ensuing battle.
Deposes Jehoahaz after 3 months, fines Judah 100 talents of silver and a talent of gold, makes Eliakim king in his place and renames him Jehoiakim; carries Jehoahaz to Egypt.

funFacts: Spans two different kings' reigns - promoted to his own tier since his role is load-bearing across both transitions.

characters.name: Jehoahaz

verses.note: Made king by the people of the land; reigns only 3 months before Necho deposes him, fines Judah, and carries him captive to Egypt.

funFacts: CRITICAL: shares the name "Jehoahaz" with the alternate name of Ahaziah, King of Judah (21:17) - a different king, three generations earlier.

characters.name: Jehoiakim

verses.note: Reigns 11 years, does evil; Nebuchadnezzar binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon and takes vessels from the Temple.

funFacts: Originally named Eliakim; renamed "Jehoiakim" by Pharaoh Necho (36:4).

characters.name: Nebuchadnezzar, King of Babylon

verses.note: Comes against Jehoiakim, binds him, takes Temple vessels to Babylon.
Sends for and brings Jehoiachin to Babylon with more Temple vessels; makes Zedekiah king in his place.
Sends the Chaldean army to destroy Jerusalem and the Temple after Zedekiah's rebellion; carries the survivors captive to Babylon.

funFacts: Central antagonist across three successive kings' reigns - promoted to his own tier rather than repeated as a submanager under each.

characters.name: Jehoiachin

verses.note: Reigns only 3 months and 10 days; carried to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar along with Temple vessels; Zedekiah made king "his brother" in his place.

funFacts: This translation's own text gives his age as "eight years old" (36:9), conflicting with 2 Kings 24:8's "eighteen" - a well-known textual crux, hedged not resolved.

characters.name: Zedekiah

genealogy.father: Josiah (per genealogical reckoning elsewhere in scripture, making him Jehoiakim's brother and Jehoiachin's uncle)

verses.note: Made king by Nebuchadnezzar at 21; rebels against him and stiffens his neck against the LORD.
Along with the priests and people, pollutes the Temple and mocks the LORD's messengers, until there is "no remedy."
Jerusalem and the Temple are destroyed by the Chaldeans; the land lies desolate to fulfil the word by Jeremiah's mouth.

funFacts: CRUX confirmed present: this translation's own text at 36:10 calls him Jehoiachin's "brother" when made king, though elsewhere understood as his uncle - hedged, not silently resolved.
The last king of Judah in this book's narrative.

characters.name: Cyrus, King of Persia

verses.note: His spirit is stirred by the LORD to fulfil Jeremiah's word; issues a proclamation permitting the exiles to return and rebuild the Temple at Jerusalem - the book's closing verses.

funFacts: The book ends mid-proclamation, on an upward, hopeful note despite the preceding destruction.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/unresolved references, kept out of the character list above, confirmed present in this translation's own text exactly matching the KJV parallels found in the existing 2Chronicles.json.
genealogyLists.hezekiah_temple_cleansing_levites_29_12_: 14-name list of Levites who cleanse the Temple (29:12-14): Mahath, Joel, Kish, Azariah (son of Jehalelel), Joah, Eden, Shimri, Jeiel, Zechariah, Mattaniah, Jehiel, Shimei, Shemaiah, Uzziel. 'Jehalelel' is the father of Azariah, not a 15th name. Undifferentiated group; no separate character entries.
genealogyLists.jehoram_slain_brothers_21_2_4: Jehoram of Judah's six brothers, killed by him on taking the throne (21:2-4): Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah, all sons of Jehoshaphat. Two of the six are BOTH named 'Azariah' within the single verse 21:2, confirmed present in this translation.
genealogyLists.josiah_huldah_delegation_34_20: The full delegation Josiah sends to inquire of the LORD via Huldah (34:20): Hilkiah, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Abdon the son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah a servant of the king's. Only Hilkiah and Shaphan the scribe get full character entries; the other three appear only as part of this single collective errand.
genealogyLists.prophetic_source_citations: Iddo the seer (9:29, 12:15, 13:22) and Nathan the prophet (9:29) are cited only as historiographic sources for the formulaic 'the rest of the acts of...are written in the book of...' pattern - pure transmission, no personally-embodied scene, so not given individual character entries.
genealogyLists.manasseh_territorial_name_note: 'Manasseh' is used as a tribal/territorial name at 31:1 and 34:6, distinct from King Manasseh (his own manager tier, ch.33).
genealogyLists.pekah_king_of_israel_note: Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, is named at 28:6 as slaying 120,000 men of Judah in one day - a single summary statistic with no scene or dialogue, so noted here rather than given a separate entry.
